title: Time Tracking Tools Pricing Guide for 2026
description: A pricing and feature comparison of time tracking platforms including Toggl, Harvest, Clockify, RescueTime, and Timely, covering billable hour tracking, team monitoring, and reporting capabilities.
body:
Time tracking software serves two distinct audiences: freelancers who need to track billable hours accurately, and organizations that want to understand how their teams spend time. The pricing for time tracking tools reflects these different use cases, with freelancer-friendly flat fees and per-user pricing for teams.

This guide examines the pricing models and feature sets of five time tracking platforms. None have published pricing verification data, so check each vendor's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Toggl Track

Toggl Track is the most widely used time tracking application, known for its one-click timer, cross-platform availability, and simple interface. The platform serves both individual freelancers and teams.

Toggl's free plan provides unlimited time tracking for individuals with basic reporting. Paid plans add team management, billable rate tracking, project dashboards, and integration with project management tools.

Toggl's pricing for freelancers uses a flat fee model that is cost-effective regardless of hours tracked. Team pricing is per user, with costs scaling linearly with team size.

Check Toggl's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Harvest

Harvest combines time tracking with invoicing and expense tracking, making it particularly valuable for service-based businesses that bill clients by the hour. Time entries flow directly into invoices, eliminating manual billing effort.

Harvest's time tracking features include a timer and manual entry, weekly timesheet views, and mobile time capture. The platform also provides expense tracking with receipt capture and mileage tracking capabilities.

Harvest's pricing uses a per-user model with a flat monthly fee that includes a set number of users. Additional users add incremental cost. The platform also offers a free plan for one user with two projects.

Check Harvest's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Clockify

Clockify offers a generous free plan with unlimited users and time tracking functionality, making it the most cost-effective option for teams of any size. The platform generates revenue through paid add-ons and premium features.

Clockify's free plan includes unlimited time tracking, unlimited users, standard reporting, and basic project management features. Paid plans add advanced reporting, audit logs, and administrator controls.

Clockify is best suited for organizations that want robust time tracking with minimal software cost. The free plan covers most common time tracking needs for small to mid-market teams.

Check Clockify's current pricing page for exact rates.

## RescueTime

RescueTime focuses on automatic time tracking and productivity analysis rather than manual time entry. The platform runs in the background, tracking application and website usage, and provides detailed reports on how time is spent.

RescueTime's automatic tracking eliminates the need for users to start and stop timers. The platform categorizes activities by productivity level, identifies distracting applications, and provides weekly productivity summaries.

RescueTime uses a subscription model with a free tier for basic automatic tracking. Paid plans add detailed reports, goal setting, and focus time features.

Check RescueTime's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Timely

Timely combines automatic time tracking with AI-powered time sheet generation and project budgeting. Its Memory feature automatically captures work activity, which users can then review, edit, and approve for accurate time sheets.

Timely's AI-generated time sheets reduce the manual effort of time tracking while maintaining accuracy through user review and approval. The platform also provides budget tracking and utilization reporting.

Timely's pricing is per user, with costs varying based on features selected. The automatic tracking feature requires higher-tier paid plans.

Check Timely's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Selection Guidance

The right time tracking platform depends on tracking methodology preference and organizational needs. Toggl is best for teams that prefer manual timer-based tracking. Harvest suits service businesses that need integrated invoicing. Clockify offers the most generous free plan for cost-conscious teams. RescueTime provides automatic tracking for productivity analysis. Timely delivers AI-powered time sheet generation for organizations that want accuracy without manual entry.
author: PilotStack Team
